limitations: Diagnostics only: BeastXPy does not claim or assert convergence. A 'pass' verdict means no user-configured diagnostic threshold was crossed, not that the MCMC converged.
BeastXPy does not perform model selection; assess never compares models, marginal likelihoods or Bayes factors (see the separate compare command).
ESS, ACT, PSRF (Gelman-Rubin R-hat) and ASDSF are finite-sample estimates; on short chains they are noisy and must not be read as proof of convergence or divergence.
Statistics whose input columns or chains are missing are reported as not_computable with a reason; BeastXPy never substitutes a guessed value.
This report describes one workdir as recorded on disk. It is not evidence of convergence, of mixing, or of model adequacy.
When no assessment document is present the assess section says 'not assessed'. BeastXPy never estimates, interpolates or back-fills ESS, PSRF, ASDSF or a verdict.
Gate statuses are derived from the artefacts in the workdir. Gates marked 'passed (inferred)' were not recorded by a gate run; the basis column states exactly which artefact implies them.
Trace statistics are computed by beastxpy.tracestats with its own ACT/ESS estimator; they are diagnostics, and short chains give uninformative intervals rather than wrong ones.
A completed BEAST run is execution evidence only. It does not mean the model is identifiable, that the calibrations are justified, or that the chain sampled the posterior adequately.
The file manifest hashes what was on disk when the report was generated. Later runs, --resume or manual edits invalidate it.
Embedded configuration text is quoted verbatim from the workdir. BeastXPy does not reconstruct a configuration that was not stored there.
The HTML is self-contained on purpose: no script, no stylesheet, no font and no image is loaded from anywhere, so the document cannot call home.
